correctness.rationale: Each source failure term f_j S_{3-j} and each withdrawn-survivor term S_1 S_2 contains alpha^4/(1+alpha)^2. Counting those factors gives the exact model likelihood. The printed Eq. (3.1) has ratio alpha^{-4R}(1+alpha)^{-2m} to that likelihood, whereas exponentiating Eq. (3.2) reproduces the model likelihood. Eq. (4.2) explicitly inherits Eq. (3.1), so its posterior needs the reciprocal alpha^{4R}(1+alpha)^{2m} factor. The packaged checker independently verifies all three kernels and the numeric score effect.

value.rationale: Bayesian inference is one of the paper's main contributions, and Eq. (4.2) is the stated target for posterior expectations, credible intervals, Tierney–Kadane approximation, and Metropolis–Hastings sampling. The missing factor depends strongly on alpha and on the censoring amount, so it cannot be dismissed as a typographical normalization. The exact correction restores compatibility between the Bayesian section and the model's own likelihood while cleanly separating theory from unavailable implementation.
